title: Read the source
intro: The application needs a runbook. The database is the source of record: it holds the saved revision.
takeaway: A normal source read asks the database for the current record. The animation uses illustrative times.

beats.text: The application needs a runbook. The database stores the saved record.
It sends a read to the database. The database looks up the key.
The database returns revision 1. The application receives the record.
Every read can repeat that work. A cache can keep a reusable copy.

title: A cache hit
intro: A cache is a separate store for reusable copies. In cache-aside, the application checks it before reading the source.
takeaway: A hit means the requested key was found in the cache. It does not establish that the copy is fresh.

beats.text: A cache holds a reusable copy. The application checks it first.
The requested key is present. This lookup is a cache hit.
The cache returns revision 1. No database read is needed here.
A hit avoids this source read. But is the copy still current?

title: A cache miss
intro: When the key is absent, the application reads the database and fills the cache. The cache does not fetch the data by itself.
takeaway: A miss is an absent key, not a failed database. Application code performs the source read and cache fill.

beats.text: The application checks the cache. The key is absent: a miss.
The application reads the source. The database has revision 1.
The database returns the record. The application receives it next.
The application fills the cache. A later lookup can find this copy.

title: A stale copy
intro: An editor updates the database, but the cached key is not deleted. A later hit can still return the old runbook.
takeaway: Source writes and cache changes are separate operations. A successful hit can still return stale data.

beats.text: Both stores begin at revision 1. The copies agree for now.
An editor saves revision 2. The cached copy is unchanged.
The next lookup checks the cache. It still finds revision 1.
The old copy returns successfully. A cache hit does not mean fresh.

title: Invalidate and refill
intro: Invalidation removes the cached key. The next reader misses, reads revision 2 from the source, and stores it.
takeaway: This repairs the illustrated stale key. Failed deletions and concurrent readers or writers need additional handling.

beats.text: The source is now at revision 2. Remove its stale cached key.
The next cache lookup misses. Read the source again.
The source returns revision 2. The application uses the new record.
Store the new copy in the cache. Concurrent writes still need care.
